items.front: Innermost layer of the Earth and its composition?
items.back: Core = NIFE (nickel + iron); outer core molten, inner core solid.
items.examPoint: Earth's internal layers — crust, mantle, core (depths & states)

items.front: SIAL vs SIMA — composition and which crust?
items.back: SIAL = silica+aluminium, granitic continental crust (~2.7); SIMA = silica+magnesium, basaltic oceanic crust (~3.0).
items.examPoint: SIAL-SIMA-NIFE composition; oceanic vs continental crust

items.front: Which discontinuity separates crust from mantle?
items.back: Mohorovicic (Moho). Others: Conrad (within crust), Repetti (mantle), Gutenberg (mantle/core), Lehmann (outer/inner core).
items.examPoint: Interior discontinuities — Conrad, Moho, Repetti, Gutenberg, Lehmann

items.front: Continental Drift — proposer, supercontinent, key fossil evidence?
items.back: Alfred Wegener (1912); Pangaea in Panthalassa; Glossopteris flora & Mesosaurus fossils.
items.examPoint: Continental Drift Theory (Wegener) — Pangaea, Tethys & evidences

items.front: Sea-floor spreading proposer and its proof?
items.back: Harry Hess; proven by symmetrical paleomagnetic stripes across mid-ocean ridges. Holmes gave convection currents.

items.front: Three plate boundary types with an example each?
items.back: Divergent = mid-ocean ridge/E. African Rift; Convergent = trench/Himalaya; Transform = San Andreas Fault.

items.front: When did the Indian Plate collide with Asia, and what else did it form?
items.back: Collision 40–50 mya raised the (still-rising) Himalayas; the same movement erupted the Deccan Traps (~60 mya).
items.examPoint: Movement of the Indian Plate — Himalayas & Deccan Traps

items.front: Focus vs epicentre of an earthquake?
items.back: Focus (hypocentre) = point inside Earth where energy is released; epicentre = surface point directly above it.

items.front: Which seismic wave proves the outer core is molten, and which is most destructive?
items.back: S-waves cannot pass liquids (molten outer core); slowest surface (L) waves are most destructive. P-waves fastest.
items.examPoint: Seismic waves — P, S and surface (L) wave characteristics

items.front: Richter scale: energy jump per step and for M5→M7?
items.back: One step ≈ 32× more energy; two steps (M5→M7) ≈ 1,000×. Mercalli measures intensity, not energy.
items.examPoint: Earthquake measurement — Richter vs Mercalli & energy scaling

items.back: Shield (fluid basalt, gentle), Composite/strato (viscous, steep), Caldera (collapse, most explosive), Flood basalt (Deccan Traps).
items.examPoint: Volcano types — shield, composite, caldera, flood basalt

items.front: Metamorphic pairs: limestone, sandstone, coal, granite become?
Signature erosional landforms of glacier, wind and karst?
items.back: Glacier = cirque/arete/horn/fjord; wind = yardang/inselberg (barchan deposits); karst = sinkhole, stalactite/stalagmite.
items.examPoint: Glacial landforms — cirque, U-valley, arete, horn, fjord, moraine, esker, drumlin

items.front: Four mountain types with an example each?
items.back: Fold = Himalayas/Alps; Block = Black Forest/Vosges; Volcanic = Kilimanjaro/Fujiyama; Residual = Aravalli.
items.examPoint: Mountain types — fold, block, volcanic, residual (world & India)
